reasoning: Recent Maine Senate polling in the last 45 days shows a very tight race, with Troy Jackson leading Susan Collins by 2 to 4 points in multiple surveys and several reports characterizing the race as a toss-up or statistical tie. The state’s Cook PVI is D+6, indicating Maine leans Democratic structurally even though the Senate contest itself remains close.

sources.name: Fox News Poll
sources.details: Fox News reported Troy Jackson ahead of Susan Collins 48% to 46% among Maine registered voters, a 2-point Jackson lead within the poll's margin of error.

sources.name: University of New Hampshire Pine Tree State Poll
sources.details: The University of New Hampshire Pine Tree State Poll found Jackson leading Collins 49% to 46% among likely general election voters.

sources.name: Hart Research / Senate Majority PAC Poll
sources.details: Hart Research's Senate Majority PAC poll showed Jackson at 49% and Collins at 45% among likely voters, a 4-point Democratic lead.

sources.name: Axios
sources.details: Reporting on the race described it as a toss-up, reflecting that neither side has established a durable lead.

sources.name: Cook Political Report (as quoted in coverage)
sources.details: Coverage noted Cook Political Report rates the Maine Senate race as a toss-up, which is a neutral competitive rating rather than a partisan lead.
